summary:
Round 3 is applied and `lune run scripts/verify` is green (596 pass, 0 fail, 0 skip, exit 0). Nothing is committed and Studio was not touched.

**What I applied**
- V1's fixAB, both parts (i) and (ii), in Cover and in CoverBrute, plus its band tests.
- V1's fixW, the Wedge rank, with its test. Another writing of one solid with different rank keys exists only for the Wedge: a Block's 24 writings tie, a Cylinder's or Ball's volume depends only on the solid, and a CornerWedge has one writing.
- V2's VerdictPrecision change (CLEANED_UNDER 0.04, its comment, the case name and T-PHY-09). It passes on the default seed and on all five other seeds.
- Every minor as tried: V1's three cap-stop tests, the thin-hider text, V2's closed-form strip, the corner-sliver text, the stale texts, and `fix2/bc.luau`'s `Worst.tooComplex`.

**Rule A: why I added it**
Tried wider, fixAB's hull rule (ii) only closes V1's own case. The hull stands out of the true patch by the patch's own sagitta (up to 0.0607 r). Closer to the surface, wholly-inside fillers still read 2–5.6 %. In F5 and F3 swords, 7 of 57 designs moved a tier (Sharpening 0.0989 → 0.296 Hard).

The cheapest exact closure is a part-level test, `Cover.farthest`. A round part whose true solid lies in a round hider's, by the buried/coincident margin, shows nothing:
- exact for a Ball, and for a Cylinder in a Ball;
- for a Cylinder in a Cylinder, exact when the axes are parallel and an upper bound otherwise.

CoverBrute does the same test independently. Afterwards none of the 6,875 placements tried reads 1 %, and the swords match the truth. The tied-axis copy now reads 0 instead of 41.8 % / 47.3 %, and `a1d`'s hidden-copy case is gone.

**Still open: round filler that pokes a hair out**
A Ball poking out of a round part by a hair (truly showing under 2 %) still reads 2.0–7.1 % and is kept. In 45 constructed F5 swords, 12 move a tier; the base does the same. I tried two rules and adopted neither:
- **Moved half-spaces wherever a facet vertex is buried:** cleans a plausible design's ball rivet that truly shows 6.3 %, and costs P4 19 % more units.
- **Hiding a facet whose vertices alone lie inside:** leaves 5 of 45 swords with a wrong tier, in either direction.

**Bit-compare against round 3's base**
On all 33,389 plausible designs, the 1,340-design corpus and the 193 fixture-set designs, no verdict, measure, mass report, owned volume or volume probe moves. Only units move, on 21,070, 1,199 and 57 designs, and no design crosses the cap. A spot re-run of the final tree reproduces this byte for byte. The plausible set's highest cleaned true share (3.615 %) and lowest kept (2.002 %) are unchanged.

I re-pinned every unit count that moved, re-timed `worst_designs.luau` (valid designs re-sorted slowest first, all under the cap), and rewrote the SPEC and E-S2.12 texts to match. The round's scripts, logs and the two rejected rules as diffs are in `docs/spec/prototypes/S2/cover/fix3/`.

deviations: I added a rule beyond fixAB: a part-level test (`Cover.farthest`, with an independent `standsOut` in CoverBrute). Without it, fixAB's hull rule leaves round filler wholly inside a round hider, near its surface, reading 2–5.6 % and moving tiers. It is exact for a Ball and for a Cylinder in a Ball. For a Cylinder in a Cylinder it is exact for parallel axes and an upper bound otherwise.
The tied-axis copy text says what the code now does: the copy reads nothing. V1's 'up to about half (41.8 %, 47.3 %)' is kept as what the models alone read, both in §4.4 and in E-S2.12.

Not closed: round filler that pokes a hair out of a round part's true surface (12 of 45 constructed swords move a tier, as on the base). The two rules I tried both fail the plausible-set bar, so I recorded it as open for the lead with numbers rather than adopt one.

V1's measured price for (i) understated it. In a valid sword, blocks straddling F5's big pommel and its grip, truly up to 11.7 %, are cleaned (no tier). Past the hitbox the price reaches 33.6 % (Ball r 3).

worst_designs.luau: no design passed the cap, so none moved to tooComplex. I re-timed its valid designs (quiet machine) and re-sorted them slowest first: tclimb_3 #3 now comes before tclimb_2 #4, and tclimb_4 #5 before #4. The SPEC's cluster and climbed-design timings, and O7's '≈ 82 / 99 ms Studio', are updated to this measurement (≈ 78 / 94); the previous numbers stay in E-S2.12's history.
V1's wedgetest.py compares vertices index by index, which fails because the two writings list them in different orders. I used the nearest-vertex set comparison from V1's fixW tree instead.
The hull test and the part test each charge UNITS_PER_TEST per point and per part, as V1 did. Building the hull adds no model units.
openIssues: Decision for the lead (blocker class): round filler in a Ball's or Cylinder's band that pokes a hair out of its true surface, or straddles it and another part, can still be kept. 12 of 45 constructed F5 swords move Sharpening to Hard. The options and their prices are in E-S2.12 and §17.2: the vertex-witness rule (cleans a plausible rivet truly 6.3 %, P4 +19 % units, the cluster past the cap), the vertices-alone rule, a finer model (2–6× cost), or curved pieces (not polygonal, and §4.1 allows no trigonometry).

Accepted price of (i): flat faces standing out of a round hider by less than its over are buried. In swords, parts that truly show 5–12 % are cleaned (no tier found; no plausible, corpus or fixture verdict moves).
Rule A for a Cylinder tilted in a Cylinder uses a bound (the caps' centres' distance + r). A tilted rod within about r·(1 − cos θ) of the hider's side falls back to the facet reading.
Not re-measured this round: checkpoint gaps; no mutation pass of my own (V1's '16 of 83 survivors killed' is V1's count); no Studio timing. S-PAR-01 is still open.
Units grow where flat faces meet round hiders: F3 +19 %, cages up to ×1.99. No cost change past noise was measured on a quiet machine.
For M3: the plausible cleaned/kept extremes are unchanged (3.615 % / 2.002 %). E-S2.12's history sections still quote the old units and timings, labelled by round.
